data.name: Urmila
data.gender_notes: Urmila is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit urmī, 'wave' — Urmilā, 'enchantress'. Its root is Sanskrit urmī (ऊर्मि). Urmila, wife of Lakshmana in the Ramayana. Urmila is a Sanskrit name meaning “Enchantress; (also) a wave”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Urmila expresses “Enchantress; (also) a wave”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Urmila total 29, reducing to 2. Number 2 is associated with cooperation, sensitivity and balance.

vedic_reference.note: Urmila is a name with deep roots in Hindu mythology and Vedic tradition. In the Mahabharata, Urmila is the wife of Lakshmana, the younger brother of Lord Rama. She is also mentioned in various other Hindu texts and puranas, where she is revered as a symbol of beauty, grace, and devotion.
